# sealift

> Prepares npm dependency updates for air-gapped networks. On the connected side, it analyses a project's package.json with pnpm and Trivy, ranks the newer versions of each direct dependency by known CVEs, proposes the oldest version that fixes the most, and packs the chosen versions into packages_npm.tar.gz for a Nexus import on the air-gapped side. One Go binary with a React interface, shipped as the image ghcr.io/morgankryze/sealift for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. GPL-3.0.

Limits: npm only. Input is a package.json whose direct dependencies are pinned to exact versions; no lockfile, workspaces, overrides or resolutions. Only direct dependencies get new versions; transitive ones change through them, without the minimum release age. The archive holds only the changed dependencies' trees. A session keeps the target platform it started with. Each export carries manifest.json.sig, an Ed25519 signature of manifest.json made with a key sealift generates for its volume; the import trusts one public key carried once to its settings (publicKeyFile). The signature does not show who asked for an export or how old it is, and the reports are not signed. A regenerated key or a lost volume means carrying a new public key. sealift has no login. A malicious package with no published CVE is not detected.

Defaults: minimum release age 14 days (range 1 to 90), resolve parallelism 4 (1 to 16), download parallelism 16 (1 to 32), target Linux x64 glibc with Node 22.17.1, pnpm 10.34.5.

## Docs

- [Overview](docs/overview.md): the two roles, context and crossing diagrams, the collection and import pipelines, what each check proves, the /data layout, a glossary
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): docker run, the setup screen, a first archive from a five-dependency project
- [Workflow](docs/workflow.md): each screen of a session with every button label
- [How sealift chooses](docs/how-sealift-chooses.md): CVE vectors by severity, tie-breaks, the eight signals, the minimum release age, the review groups
- [Settings](docs/settings.md): target platform, Node version, signing key, limits, Trivy updates, the settings API
- [The air gap](docs/air-gap.md): the archive, the signature and the trusted key, the reports, sha256 checks, the import, lockfile drift
- [Importing](docs/importing.md): the import service screens: Archives, Imports and one import, the trusted key, every state and the retry card
- [Deployment](docs/deployment.md): hardened Compose, capabilities, reverse proxy with SSE, outbound hosts, the /data volume, the key the import trusts, upgrades, backups
- [Runbook](docs/runbook.md): both sides from nothing to a first import: the drop-in values, Harbor, the Secret, the ingress and oauth2-proxy values, a checklist, upgrades, backups, the worst cases on a shared Nexus repository and the rollback list
- [Helm chart](docs/helm.md): the chart of the import service, every value, the `token.header` setting, the install notes, Argo CD and the release
- [Request to the administrators](docs/admin-request.md): the MinIO, Nexus and Keycloak accounts and the infrastructure the install needs, with the reason for each
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): each message with its cause and fix
- [FAQ](docs/faq.md): lockfiles, transitive dependencies, other ecosystems, data, reset
